Article Title: 'Is it okay?' PM Modi pauses speech as Xi appears uncomfortable; Chinese president skips gala dinner
Article Text:
Xi was visiting India for the first time in seven years.

Modi, Xi discuss future of bilateral ties

Border, trade issues on agenda

Three ‘mutuals’ guide ties

Xi skips gala dinner

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi briefly interrupted his opening remarks at the Brics Summit on Saturday after Chinese President Xi Jinping appeared to be uncomfortable.PM Modi turned towards Xi and asked the translator accompanying the Chinese president, “Is it okay?” He repeated the question moments later.It was not immediately clear what had caused Xi’s apparent discomfort. It may have been related to the microphone or the translation of PM Modi’s remarks. There was no immediate official reaction from China.The footage of the speech, shared by Doordarshan, shows the incident between the 4:30- and 5-minute marks. Xi, who was visiting India for the first time in seven years, later attended the Brics Summit and held bilateral talks with PM Modi.During their 40-minute meeting on the sidelines of the Brics Summit, the two leaders agreed that India and China should take a strategic and long-term view of their relationship and ensure that differences do not turn into disputes.Xi said the current momentum in bilateral ties, built on the resumption of institutional exchanges, an expanding cooperation agenda and growing trade, had been hard-won and should be cherished.PM Modi welcomed the “steady progress” in relations but underlined that peace and tranquillity in border areas would remain an essential basis for the continued development of bilateral ties.The meeting was the leaders’ third bilateral interaction in two years, following their meetings in Kazan in 2024 and Tianjin last year. It was also their first meeting on Indian soil in seven years.Xi reiterated that India and China were partners, not rivals. However, the Indian readout did not include that formulation.PM Modi stressed the need for both sides to honour existing agreements and understandings on border-related issues.The Indian side said the leaders reaffirmed their commitment to finding a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable solution to the boundary question, keeping in mind the broader political perspective of bilateral ties and the long-term interests of both countries.Modi also raised India’s trade deficit with China and called for greater predictability in supply chains and meaningful, predictable market access.The two sides discussed the need to address concerns related to structural trade imbalances, supply chains and economic cooperation.Since the 2024 Kazan meeting, which marked the end of the eastern Ladakh border standoff, three rounds of talks between the Special Representatives of India and China have taken place. At their latest meeting, the two sides agreed to work towards an early and substantial outcome on boundary delimitation and border management.The leaders also noted progress in people-to-people relations and stressed the need to promote cultural exchanges, business ties and greater mobility.“Prime Minister highlighted that both sides must be guided by three mutuals- mutual respect, mutual sensitivity and mutual interest,” the Indian readout said.They also agreed to expand common ground on regional and global issues and cooperate in addressing shared challenges.Xi called for a more rational and forward-looking strategic assessment of bilateral relations, win-win cooperation, mutual respect and understanding, and inclusive multilateral cooperation.Xi Jinping, however, did not attend a gala dinner hosted by PM Modi for Brics leaders, partner countries and representatives of international organisations, sources aware of the matter told PTI.The reason for his absence was not immediately known. A source suggested that Xi had returned to his hotel to rest after a busy day.Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed, who left for home after attending the summit, was also absent from the dinner.Russian President Vladimir Putin and other Brics leaders attended the event. Union ministers, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla and several chief ministers were also present.Union ministers at the dinner included Amit Shah, Nirmala Sitharaman, Piyush Goyal, Ashwini Vaishnaw and Shivraj Singh Chouhan. Chief ministers Yogi Adityanath, Devendra Fadnavis, Suvendu Adhikari and Himanta Biswa Sarma also attended.The ministers and chief ministers travelled in two buses from Parliament House to Bharat Mandapam, where the dinner was held.The dinner menu featured khandvi mille-feuille, khumb galouti, paneer lababdar, gucchi marmik, carrot-bean poriyal and millet pulao.The dessert menu included Old Delhi fruit cream with jalebi and shahtoot phirni. India is hosting the Brics Summit on September 12-13, with leaders from the 11 member countries and 10 partner countries, along with representatives of international organisations, attending the event.
Article Summary: PM Modi briefly interrupted his opening remarks at the Brics Summit on Saturday after Chinese President Xi Jinping appeared to be uncomfortable. Xi was visiting India for the first time in seven years. It was not immediately clear what had caused Xi’s apparent discomfort.

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Sunday met Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim over breakfast on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi.Congress general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra was also present at the meeting. Pictures shared by the Congress showed Rahul Gandhi and Anwar Ibrahim engaged in conversation over breakfast, with the two also seen shaking hands and exchanging smiles.Ibrahim later described Rahul Gandhi as his "good friend" in a post on X, saying the meeting provided an opportunity to exchange views on developments around the world and in the region."Had the opportunity once again to meet my good friend, who is also the Leader of the Opposition in the Indian Parliament, Rahul Gandhi, this morning over breakfast. This brief meeting provided space for us to exchange views on the latest international and regional developments," the Malaysian prime minister said.The meeting came a day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi held talks with Ibrahim on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit. Their discussions focused on strengthening cooperation in areas including trade, semiconductors, infrastructure and defence.Malaysia is a partner country in the BRICS grouping and is also an important partner for India within the ASEAN framework.The breakfast meeting took place as the BRICS Summit entered its final day, with leaders gathering at Bharat Mandapam for an open session on ‘Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability: Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth’.The summit has focused heavily on global geopolitical and economic challenges. The New Delhi Declaration 2026, adopted on Saturday, expressed deep concern over the escalation of tensions in West Asia and called for maximum restraint.Addressing the summit on Sunday, PM Modi said rising geopolitical tensions were adversely affecting ordinary people across the world and called for greater BRICS cooperation to tackle challenges facing the Global South.He also raised concerns over the "weaponisation of technology and critical minerals", saying such developments could hinder shared progress and prosperity.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday warned against the weaponisation of technology and critical minerals, saying that there is a need for inclusivity in the adoption of technology.During his closing remarks on the second day of the Brics summit, PM Modi said that tightening control over technology and critical minerals could hinder shared progress of countries."Under the umbrella of innovation, the Brics Incubator Network will connect our startups and incubators. We have proposed the Brics Startup Innovation Fund to promote innovative and scalable solutions. The Brics Network on Digital Agriculture will create new opportunities for farmers; through this initiative, AI, geospatial technology, and digital public infrastructure will be aligned with the actual needs of farmers. The weaponisation of technology and critical minerals could hinder our shared progress; therefore, we have emphasised inclusivity in the adoption of technology,” PM Modi said.“The strength of Brics lies in our diversity and cooperation. We may be rooted in different realities, but together we rise through cooperation and blossom for humanity. May our diversity remain our identity, our cooperation serve as our inspiration, and our progress benefit all of humanity," he added.Interestingly, the remarks were made in the presence of Chinese President Xi Jinping. Although the Prime Minister did not name any particular country, the remarks can be seen as a message to Beijing, which holds a dominant position in global supply chains for critical minerals and rare earths.Last year, China tightened its export controls on rare earths and other materials critical for advanced tech manufacturing during trade negotiations with the United States.China controls more than 90 percent of global rare-earth refining, giving it enormous leverage over critical technologies, from the permanent magnets used in EVs and AI data centres to components in advanced electronics and semiconductors.During his address, PM Modi also said that “India has advanced the spirit of friendship, partnership, and cooperation through the Brics platform.”“We have endeavoured to ensure that Brics cooperation is not limited to governments alone; we want our entrepreneurs, farmers, researchers, women, youth, and ordinary citizens to become active participants as well,” PM Modi said."I can say from personal experience that the trust of Global South nations in Brics has grown, because their voices are heard, their experiences are respected, and solutions are crafted not just for them, but with them. The strength of Brics lies in our diversity and cooperation. We may be rooted in different realities, but together we rise through cooperation and blossom for humanity. May our diversity remain our identity, our cooperation serve as our inspiration, and our progress benefit all of humanity," he added.The last leg of the summit focused on the core pillars of India's 2026 Brics chairship -- resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability. The two-day summit is being hosted by India on September 12-13 under the chairship theme, “Building for resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability."The open session is part of the two-day Brics summit being hosted by India on September 12-13 under the chairship theme, “Building for resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability."
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi warned against the weaponisation of technology and critical minerals. Remarks were made in the presence of Chinese President Xi Jinping. The remarks can be seen as a message to Beijing, which holds a dominant position in global supply chains for critical minerals and rare earths.

Article Title: 'Stronger India-China ties strategically important for Global South': Chinese journalist at Brics summit 2026

Stronger India-China ties are strategically important for the two countries and the wider Global South, a Chinese journalist said on Sunday, a day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping reaffirmed their commitment to stabilising bilateral relations on the sidelines of the Brics summit in New Delhi.Speaking to news agency ANI, Qingduo U, a journalist with Chinese state broadcaster CGTN, said the size of India and China’s populations and economies made their relationship one of the world’s most consequential.“China and India probably have the most consequential relationship in the world, as well as in BRICS,” he said, stressing that both countries needed to stabilise their ties and take a long-term view of the relationship.He welcomed the Brics push for a more representative global order, saying the rise of the Global South made greater representation in institutions such as the United Nations Security Council, International Monetary Fund and World Bank a “reasonable demand”.“Multipolarity, or multipolar development, is here. It’s irreversible. There’s a rise of the Global South, which is unstoppable. That’s the reality,” he said, calling for reforms to make the global order “more balanced, more representative, and more just”.On the PM Modi-Xi meeting, Qingduo said the two leaders had demonstrated a “strategic vision and long-term perspective” by stressing peace and tranquillity along the India-China border.PM Modi and President Xi on Saturday expressed commitment to a “fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable” resolution of the boundary question and agreed that bilateral ties should be viewed from a strategic and long-term perspective. PM Modi said differences between the two countries should not become disputes and that the relationship should be guided by mutual respect, sensitivity and interest, according to the ministry of external affairs.Meanwhile, Gaziza Uzak, head of Kazakhstan’s NazarMedia and a member of the country’s Union of Journalists, praised India’s leadership of the Brics summit and said the gathering offered countries an opportunity to strengthen cooperation.“We support Modi’s programme because I think he speaks more good and best information for us to save our planet and to make our lives and our relationships better,” she said.Nigerian journalist Emperor Simon of Channels Television also described the summit as an important forum for Brics members and partner countries to discuss global challenges and future cooperation.The two-day summit is being hosted by India on September 12-13 under the chairship theme, “Building for resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability."
Article Summary: Stronger India-China ties are strategically important for the two countries and the wider Global South, a Chinese journalist said. Qingduo U, a journalist with Chinese state broadcaster CGTN, said the size of India and China’s populations and economies made their relationship one of the world's most consequential. He welcomed the Brics push for a more representative global order.

Article Title: PM Modi holds talks with Ethiopia, Malaysia; defence, investment on agenda
Article Text:
Sources said the talks with Ethiopia and Malaysia marked a new trajectory in India's relations with the two countries

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi held separate bilateral meetings with Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Ali and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim in New Delhi on Saturday, with India seeking to deepen cooperation with both countries in defence, investment and emerging sectors.Sources said the talks with Ethiopia and Malaysia marked a new trajectory in India's relations with the two countries. Both expressed interest in strengthening defence cooperation with India, including joint personnel training and defence procurement, the sources said.The two countries also welcomed greater participation by Indian industry and investment. Ethiopia, in particular, expressed interest in Indian mining companies, while discussions with Malaysia covered opportunities in the semiconductor sector, according to the sources. PM Modi met Anwar on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit, where Malaysia is participating as a BRICS partner country at India's invitation. The Malaysian prime minister is scheduled to deliver a national statement on "Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth" at the summit.According to Malaysia's Foreign Ministry, the country is expected to push for stronger cooperation among BRICS members and partner countries on development challenges, economic opportunities and ensuring more inclusive access to technological advances and innovation.Anwar is also scheduled to visit Kerala, with the visit aimed at strengthening bilateral ties and expanding cooperation in areas including trade and investment, the digital economy, talent and labour, education and regional connectivity.PM Modi also met Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed at Hyderabad House. Ethiopia joined BRICS as a full member in January 2024, alongside Egypt, Iran, Saudi Arabia and the UAE.The latest talks build on growing India-Ethiopia defence engagement. Earlier this month, officials from the two countries discussed ways to expand cooperation in military training, defence industry collaboration and UN peacekeeping. The discussions also covered new and emerging areas of defence cooperation.The ministry of defence had said after the meeting between Ethiopian Charge d'Affaires Nebiyu Tedla and Defence Ministry Joint Secretary Amitabh Prasad that the two sides discussed "avenues to further strengthen India-Ethiopia defence cooperation, including training, defence industry collaboration and UN Peacekeeping, with focus on new and emerging areas."
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi held separate bilateral meetings with Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Ali and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim in New Delhi. India seeking to deepen cooperation with both countries in defence, investment and emerging sectors. Both expressed interest in strengthening defence cooperation with India.

Article Title: Yogi Adityanath pays tribute to UP's first CM Govind Ballabh Pant on his 139th birth anniversary

Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Thursday paid floral tribute to the state's first chief minister and freedom fighter Pandit Govind Ballabh Pant on his 139th birth anniversary, recalling his contributions to India's freedom struggle, governance and social reforms.Speaking at an event held to mark the birth anniversary, Yogi Adityanath described Pant as a great advocate and freedom fighter who played a significant role in the country's struggle for independence."On this occasion, on behalf of the Government of Uttar Pradesh and the revered people of Uttar Pradesh, I pay homage to the memories of Pandit Govind Ballabh Pant ji on the occasion of his auspicious birth anniversary, and offer my humble tributes," Yogi said.Recalling Pant's contribution to the Kakori case, the chief minister said that in 1925, Pant had strongly defended revolutionaries facing a case filed by the British government following the Kakori Train Action.He said Pant actively participated in the freedom movement and resigned as the Premier of Uttar Pradesh after being elected to the post in 1937, choosing instead to join the struggle against British rule."Whether it was the Quit India Movement or other major agitations from time to time for the freedom struggle, he actively took part in them," Yogi said.The Chief Minister highlighted Pant's role after Independence, saying he became the first chief minister of Uttar Pradesh in 1947, when present-day Uttarakhand was also part of the state."As the first chief minister of Uttar Pradesh... he initiated efforts to present the governance of such a large state as a model of good governance, foster its economic development, and work for the welfare of every section of society," he said.Yogi also recalled Pant's contribution to land reforms and described the model introduced during his tenure as exemplary.Later, as Union Home minister from 1954, Pant worked to address linguistic conflicts and played an important role in establishing Hindi as the official language, Yogi said."On this occasion, on behalf of the Government of Uttar Pradesh and the people of Uttar Pradesh, I pay homage to his memory and offer my humble tributes to him," the chief minister said.
Article Summary: Yogi Adityanath pays tribute to UP's first CM Govind Ballabh Pant on his 139th birth anniversary. Yogi described Pant as a great advocate and freedom fighter who played a significant role in the country's struggle for independence.

Article Title: Three years before 9/11, CIA warned Clinton that Bin Laden wanted to strike India
Article Text:
Osama bin Laden (File photo)

Three years before the 9/11 attacks shocked the United States, then-President Bill Clinton was warned by the CIA that Osama bin Laden intended to carry out attacks in India, Pakistan, Uganda and possibly Nigeria.A newly declassified CIA warning dated August 28, 1998, said Bin Laden had survived US missile strikes in Afghanistan and retained a network of individuals and allied groups across at least 60 countries that could be used to mount attacks.The assessment specifically listed India and Pakistan, along with Egypt, the Arabian Peninsula – particularly Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Yemen – Uganda and possibly Nigeria, as countries where Bin Laden intended to conduct attacks.Bin Laden also viewed India as part of what he described as a “Crusader-Zionist-Hindu” conspiracy against the Islamic world, reflecting the ideological lens through which he framed India and its relationship with the US and Israel.The CIA said Bin Laden was also considering further attacks against the US and UK, although he had not indicated precise targets or timing.The assessment came weeks after the August 1998 bombings of US embassies in Kenya and Tanzania, which killed more than 200 people and brought Bin Laden's organisation firmly into the sights of US counterterrorism agencies.The newly released document said Bin Laden’s infrastructure in North America, Europe and East Asia also lent credibility to reports that he could target US interests in those regions.The CIA assessment further noted that Bin Laden had authorised an associate to explore attacks in the US and that US officials had recently helped arrest Bin Laden operatives preparing attacks in Tirana and possibly Baku.The India reference is significant because it shows that the threat posed by Bin Laden’s network was being assessed as extending beyond the Middle East, Africa and the US well before the September 11 attacks.The August 1998 assessment was part of a series of intelligence warnings about Bin Laden that accumulated in the years before 9/11. The newly released material includes warnings about his pursuit of unconventional weapons, potential attacks on US soil and, later, the possibility of aircraft hijackings.The documents also show that Bin Laden’s network was not viewed as a purely Afghanistan-based threat. The CIA described a global infrastructure capable of supporting or inspiring attacks across multiple regions.For India, the 1998 assessment offers an early glimpse of how New Delhi had already figured in US intelligence assessments of the emerging Bin Laden threat, years before the attacks that would transform global counterterrorism policy.
Article Summary: Bin Laden viewed India as part of what he described as a “Crusader-Zionist- Hindu” conspiracy against the Islamic world. The August 1998 assessment was part of a series of intelligence warnings about Bin Laden that accumulated in the years before 9/11.

Article Title: Modi: Global South must shape, not just follow, rules
Article Text:
These should be focused on representation, responsiveness and rulemaking, PM Modi said.

Modi positions Brics as an inclusive, not anti-west, forum

NEW DELHI: Declaring the 18th Brics leaders' summit open, PM Narendra Modi stressed that UN Security Council (UNSC) reforms cannot be delayed any longer and that the "pyramid of privilege" reflected in the current global governance structure must be transformed into a "platform of partnership".Modi focused on economic integration of the Global South in his address at the session on inclusive governance and multilateralism, saying the bloc must work together to turn developing countries from rule-takers to rule-shapers."The Global South today stands in the front row of global crises, but in the back row of decision-making," the PM said, proposing that Brics draft 10 proposals for global governance reform.These should be focused on representation, responsiveness and rulemaking, PM Modi said. He sought a system “where every country has a voice, every member has a stake and the development of humanity remains at the centre of all endeavours”.Also read | Brics hammers out joint declaration after India bridges Iran-UAE chasm On representation, he said UNSC reform can no longer be delayed and text-based negotiations on this subject must be tied to a fixed timeline and clear outcomes. “Similarly, voting power, leadership positions and policy priorities within global financial institutions must reflect today’s economic realities.Countries driving global economic growth deserve an appropriate role in shaping global economic governance,” he added.While western experts have often described Brics as an anti-West forum, Modi said the grouping operates not against anyone, but with an inclusive approach that brings everyone along. “Today, Brics is also in its coming-of-age moment. Over the past 20 years, Brics has established a distinct identity on the global stage. We respect each other’s perspectives and move forward through consensus,” he said.The PM called upon the bloc to work on an ambitious new agenda, translating its unity and consensus into concrete results on the global stage. He proposed establishment of a Brics Continuity and Implementation Mechanism. “Brics presidency changes every year, but this should not disrupt our institutional momentum. Under this mechanism, all initiatives and outcomes can be followed up through the troika (past, current and incoming presidency),” said Modi.Also read | UN hails Iran-UAE meeting on sidelines of Brics Summit, says India can be 'bridge-builder' Raising the issue of seafarers’ safety, Modi talked about how they make a massive contribution to global trade and yet lack adequate support in difficult times. He proposed creating a Seafarers Emergency Support Network to connect maritime authorities and missions of relevant nations. “This network would assist with distress alerts, medical aid, family notifications and evacuation efforts.”He said ensuring equal participation in setting the global rules of the future is critical. “AI, cyberspace, outer space, biotechnology and critical technologies are shaping not only future opportunities, but also future rules. We must work to transform the Global South from rule-takers to rule-shapers,” he said. “The message of this Brics summit must be clear: if our future is shared, the right to shape it must also be shared,” he said.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi says UN Security Council (UNSC) reforms cannot be delayed any longer. He said the "pyramid of privilege" reflected in the current global governance structure must be transformed into a "platform of partnership" Modi said the bloc must work together to turn developing countries from rule-takers to rule-shapers.

Article Title: Elephant Madhuri now on her way to Kolhapur as Anant Ambani's Vantara vows continued medical care
Article Text: Madhuri, the elephant popularly known as Mahadevi in Kolhapur, will be allowed to return to the city after the High-Powered Committee (HPC) passed an order on September 9, Anant Ambani’s Vantara said in a statement on Thursday.According to Vantara, the HPC permitted Madhuri’s return after hearing the parties' claims, reviewing reports, and inspecting the facility at Nandani in Maharashtra. The order has laid down several conditions, including that Madhuri cannot be used in processions or for any other purpose.The elephant will also need round-the-clock care and a medical examination every fortnight, Vantara said.Madhuri was brought to Vantara in Jamnagar on July 30, 2025, in compliance with directions from the HPC, which the Bombay High Court and the Supreme Court upheld. Vantara said it had not sought her custody but had received and cared for her in accordance with the directions.The organisation said Madhuri’s health had stabilised after sustained veterinary care, but her chronic conditions still require supportive management and regular monitoring.As part of the transition, Vantara said it had helped arrange living conditions, veterinary infrastructure, medical equipment, medicines and other necessities at the Nandani facility. Its veterinarians will visit Madhuri in Kolhapur every fortnight to conduct her medical examination and submit reports to the competent authorities, as directed by the HPC.Vantara also said it had worked to improve the enclosure at Nandani within the available infrastructure. Further upgrades, it said, were currently restricted by town-planning constraints, including a road passing through land belonging to the trust.The organisation added that it would remain available to support future upgrades at the facility and would assist if directed by the courts or competent authorities.“Madhuri’s wellbeing remains Vantara’s first concern. Our commitment to her health, welfare and dignity does not depend on where she lives,” the statement said.
Article Summary: Madhuri, the elephant popularly known as Mahadevi in Kolhapur, will be allowed to return to the city. The High-Powered Committee (HPC) passed an order on September 9. The order has laid down several conditions, including that Madhuri cannot be used in processions or for any other purpose.

Article Title: India to get another major DRDO missile testing range in Bengal
Article Text:
The proposed testing range in Junput will be the third major hub for DRDO after the Chandipur sites and the proposed testing centre in Andhra

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a boost for the country's defence testing capabilities, India will get another weapon and missile testing range in Bengal's Junput coastal village in Purba Medinipur district.In April 2024, DRDO had proposed a testing range along the Purba Medinipur coast to complement its integrated testing range in Odisha's Chandipur. However, the then TMC govt had not given land for it. During an event Friday, CM Suvendu Adhikari revealed that DRDO had sent a letter for the project but the then TMC govt at the helm did not respond. "I have okayed it. This will be a big project for West Bengal's development," he said. A source in DRDO also confirmed to TOI that the missile testing project is coming up in Bengal.The proposed testing range in Junput will be the third major hub for DRDO after the Chandipur sites and the proposed testing centre in Andhra. India has one missile testing facility, known as the Integrated Test Range, which operates across two launch complexes in Odisha: Launch Complex-III at Chandipur-on-Sea and Launch Complex-IV, off Odisha coast.While Launch Complex-III is used primarily for testing short-range tactical missiles, surface-to-air systems and multi-barrel rocket launchers like the Akash and Pinaka, Launch Complex-IV is designated for long-range strategic weapon trials, including Agni ballistic missile series and K-series submarine-launched missiles.The Chandipur testing facility provides a secure coastal location with a wide, unobstructed eastward trajectory over the Bay of Bengal. The proposed Junput range, located approximately 70km along the Bay of Bengal from Chandipur, will share the workload of the Odisha testing range.
Article Summary: In April 2024, DRDO had proposed a testing range along the Purba Medinipur coast to complement its integrated testing range in Odisha's Chandipur. The proposed Junput range will share the workload of the Odisha testing range. India has one missile testing facility, known as the Integrated Test Range, which operates across two launch complexes.

Article Title: FSSAI orders recall of two food products
Article Text:

Article Title: Delhi 2047: The big plan, the bigger question
Article Text:

So, can MPD-2047 be sustainable?

Can the city’s infrastructure keep pace?

By 2047, Delhi could be home to nearly 32 million people, need around 1,600 million gallons of potable water every day, generate nearly 26,000 tonnes of solid waste daily and require roughly 40 lakh additional homes.Those numbers tell a bigger story than population growth. They point to a city that will need to build more — while somehow using less land, less water and fewer resources, without compromising safety, mobility, liveability or the environment.That is the challenge at the heart of the Master Plan for Delhi 2047 (MPD-2047).The Delhi Development Authority (DDA) unveiled the MPD-2047 at the National Media Centre on August 20, 2026, presenting it as the fourth master plan for the capital, with a perspective extending to 2047. The authority has described the plan as a framework for shaping Delhi’s future growth, with its focus spanning housing, mobility, infrastructure, environmental sustainability and efficient land use.The plan comes after earlier master plans for 1962, 2001 and 2021. DDA’s current master-plan framework includes policies on transit-oriented development, land pooling, redevelopment of ageing neighbourhoods and ecological restoration, placing long-term urban growth alongside infrastructure capacity and sustainability.It envisions a denser, more connected and more transit-oriented Delhi, with large-scale housing, redevelopment of ageing neighbourhoods, stronger public transport, green-blue networks, ecological restoration and new approaches to land and infrastructure planning. It also pushes for compact growth, with development increasingly tied to the capacity of roads, public transport, water, drainage, sewerage and other essential services.But there is a larger question: Can Delhi grow at this scale without repeating the problems that already make the city struggle today?The question becomes harder to ignore when incidents such as the recent Satya Niketan building collapse enter the conversation. The tragedy exposed something the master plan itself acknowledges: planning a city is not enough if building safety, approvals, enforcement and infrastructure do not keep pace with growth.So, what does MPD-2047 promise, and can Delhi actually deliver it?Housing is perhaps the plan’s biggest promise. MPD-2047 estimates the city’s housing requirement at nearly 40 lakh dwelling units by 2047. The strategy combines affordable housing, rental housing, EWS housing, hostels and dormitories, affordable rental housing complexes and redevelopment of existing areas. The government says around 18 lakh affordable homes could come through transit-oriented development, while redevelopment of existing group and government housing could add around seven lakh dwelling units.Land pooling is another major pillar, with the DDA hoping to unlock large areas of land and potentially facilitate up to 20 lakh homes.This is sensible in a land-constrained city. But “affordable” is not simply a number of units. A home is affordable only if households can afford its purchase or rent, utilities, maintenance and commute.That makes displacement an important question. Redevelopment and densification can raise land values and change neighbourhood economics. The success of the housing strategy will therefore depend not only on how many homes are built, but who can actually continue to live in them.MPD-2047 also brings Delhi’s 357 villages into the larger redevelopment conversation. At a conference organised by the Dilli Dehat Project, speakers argued that the plan treats these villages primarily as areas for “regeneration”, rather than recognising them as historic settlements with distinct social, cultural and ecological assets. They also raised concerns about the protection of village commons such as ponds and grazing land, and the impact of road widening and land pooling on existing communities.MPD-2047 moves Delhi towards more compact development. It promotes redevelopment of brownfield areas, mixed-use development and transit-oriented growth, while encouraging higher intensity around mass-transit corridors. The plan also allows buildings of more than 100 floors to be developed as landmark projects in areas with adequate infrastructure.The idea is to support compact growth, reduce urban sprawl and free up more ground-level space for public and green areas. But density is not automatically sustainable.Concentrating growth near Metro and other mass-transit corridors can also make public transport more viable. Sustainability of vertical growth will depend on what surrounds these towers — transport, water, sewage, power, fire safety and open space. Building higher can save land, but only if infrastructure rises with it.Every additional floor brings additional demand for water, sewage, electricity, roads, parking, fire services, schools, healthcare and drainage. MPD-2047 itself takes an infrastructure-led approach: new development is intended to be supported by roads, public transport, water, sewerage, drainage, power and digital connectivity.The real test, therefore, is sequencing.Can infrastructure capacity be demonstrated before density is increased?That may be one of the most important implementation questions for MPD-2047.Water may be the plan’s clearest sustainability test.In 2021, Delhi’s water supply was about 935 MGD, against estimated demand of around 1,380 MGD. By 2047, potable-water demand is projected at approximately 1,600 MGD. The detailed augmentation calculation identifies about 401 MGD of additional supply, taking projected availability from roughly 1,000 MGD to about 1,401 MGD.That leaves an apparent gap of roughly 200 MGD against the 1,600 MGD demand estimate.The figures come from different stages and assumptions within the planning calculations, so they should not be treated as a simple supply-versus-demand failure. But they do highlight a genuine vulnerability: Delhi’s future growth cannot depend on finding water after development has already happened.That leaves an apparent gap of roughly 200 MGD against the 1,600 MGD demand estimate.The figures come from different stages and assumptions within the planning calculations, so they should not be treated as a simple supply-versus-demand failure. But they do highlight a genuine vulnerability: Delhi’s future growth cannot depend on finding water after development has already happened.That leaves an apparent gap of roughly 200 MGD against the 1,600 MGD demand estimate.The figures come from different stages and assumptions within the planning calculations, so they should not be treated as a simple supply-versus-demand failure. But they do highlight a genuine vulnerability: Delhi’s future growth cannot depend on finding water after development has already happened.Water recycling, rainwater harvesting, wastewater treatment, groundwater recharge and demand management therefore need to move from supporting provisions to core infrastructure.As MoHUA secretary D Thara recently told real-estate developers, housing projects need green areas, rainwater harvesting, water recycling and sewage-treatment infrastructure rather than simply buildings and roads.The Satya Niketan building collapse has put Delhi’s student housing and building-safety systems under scrutiny. A five-storey boys’ paying guest accommodation near Delhi University’s South Campus collapsed in September 2026, killing seven people, including five university students.The wider question is how safely Delhi’s high-density neighbourhoods are being managed. In Rajendra Nagar, severe waterlogging and drainage failures have repeatedly disrupted life, while the deaths of civil-services aspirants in a flooded coaching-centre basement in 2024 exposed serious gaps in building use, drainage and enforcement. Similar concerns have emerged around cramped PGs, narrow lanes and ageing buildings in student hubs.These incidents underline that urban growth is not only about adding housing and infrastructure. As MPD-2047 enables redevelopment and greater density, building permissions, structural safety, drainage, inspections and emergency access will have to keep pace.The real question is not how high Delhi can build, but how safely it can grow.Yes — the plan has the ingredients for a more sustainable Delhi: compact growth, transit-oriented development, affordable housing, green-blue infrastructure and infrastructure-led planning.But a plan is only a framework. Its success will depend on coordinated implementation, enforcement and infrastructure capacity.The key question is simple: Can Delhi build capacity as fast as it builds density?If yes, MPD-2047 could make Delhi more connected, resilient and resource-efficient. If not, it could simply make today’s problems bigger.The plan sets the direction. Delivery will determine the outcome.
Article Summary: The Delhi Development Authority (DDA) unveiled the MPD-2047 at the National Media Centre on August 20, 2026. It is the fourth master plan for the capital, with a perspective extending to 2047. It envisions a denser, more connected and more transit-oriented Delhi, with large-scale housing.

NEW DELHI: Brics nations Saturday opposed unilateral trade measures such as EU’s carbon border adjustment mechanism (CBAM), saying such measures undermine efforts by developing countries aimed at addressing the adverse impacts of climate change.Though they recognised the need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions to meet climate goals, the grouping’s members sought to delink any unilateral punitive action from achieving a common goal and pitched for energy security for all based on a pragmatic approach where “fossil fuel”, they said, will still play an important role in the world’s energy mix”, particularly for emerging markets and developing economies, in addition to renewable sources and nuclear.CBAM, which entered its operational regime on Jan 1, is a tool to put a price, through imposing a border tax, on carbon-intensive goods, like iron and steel, aluminium and cement, that are entering the 27 EU nations.Though BRICS nations opposed the proposal from the time it was conceived, arguing that the unilateral move placed an additional burden on businesses in developing economies due to embedded emissions in their products, they made their points a part of New Delhi Declaration calling it “punitive, discriminatory and protectionist measures that are not in line with international law”.Without any attempt to dilute their respective efforts to meet climate action goals under the Paris Agreement, the nations called for greater actions based on equity and the UN’s principle of common but differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities, in light of different national circumstances.They also highlighted the need to enhance energy security by ensuring energy market stability and maintaining undisrupted flows of energy from diverse sources including fossil fuels. Incidentally, four of the BRICS group countries such as Russia, Saudi Arabia, Iran and UAE are among the major global exporters of fossil fuel.Sending a positive signal ahead of COP31, scheduled to take place in Turkey in Nov, they called on all countries to uphold their commitment to maintain and scale up efforts to combat climate change, and expressed their confidence in multilateralism to address the global challenge.

Article Title: Brics embraces AI but leaves job displacement largely unaddressed
Article Text:
Brics New Delhi Declaration backs AI-driven growth and worker re-skilling but leaves unanswered what happens to jobs lost to automation.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Brics has set out an ambitious plan to prepare people for an AI-driven economy, but its New Delhi Declaration leaves a key question largely unanswered — what happens to workers whose jobs are lost or sharply changed because of automation and AI?The declaration calls AI an “immense opportunity to stimulate economic growth and sustainable development for all” and backs wider access to AI, while stressing safety, security, inclusion and reliability. But on employment, its response is largely to prepare workers for changing skill needs rather than spell out what happens when technology replaces existing work.The declaration commits Brics countries to strengthen cooperation in “forecasting skills needs by analysing labour market trends in digital, green, care and other priority sectors”. It also welcomes Brics Connect, the “BRICS Cooperation Network for Capacity Building, Employability, and New Skills and Technologies”, focused on skills for changing labour markets.The declaration addresses some changes already taking place. It calls for nationally tailored approaches to expand social protection for gig and platform workers and recognises the need to protect workers moving across borders, including through portability of benefits. It also notes an initiative to establish an “International Digital Platform for Remote Employment” for Brics countries.But there is no equivalent, specific commitment on workers whose existing jobs may disappear because of AI.The declaration does not propose a Brics system to identify occupations exposed to automation, provide transition support to affected workers or measure AI-related job losses.That gap stands out because Brics is simultaneously encouraging wider use of AI across its economies. Its Centre for Industrial Competencies supports manufacturing companies, including SMEs, in adopting Industry 4.0 and advanced digital production technologies, including AI.Brics does recognise some AI-related risks beyond employment. In the intellectual property section, it notes “risks relating to misappropriation and misrepresentation of knowledge, heritage, and cultural values” that are insufficiently represented in datasets and AI models.For workers the declaration promises labour markets that are “future-ready”, “ensuring that no worker is left behind”.
Article Summary: Brics New Delhi Declaration backs AI-driven growth and worker re-skilling. But it leaves unanswered what happens to jobs lost to automation. declaration commits Brics countries to strengthen cooperation in “forecasting skills needs by analysing labour market trends”

NEW DELHI: Brics countries want to bring education and jobs closer together, with a new focus on STEM, vocational training, digital skills and AI, while also trying to identify what skills employers will need in the coming years.The New Delhi Declaration links the entire chain — from basic learning and digital literacy to higher education, technical training and jobs. The declaration seeks to connect what students learn with what factories, businesses and other employers will need — while using labour-market trends to keep training relevant as technology changes.

NEW DELHI: Congress on Saturday took a jab at the Centre by invoking the iconic Bollywood melody, “Tu jahan jahan chale ga, mera saaya saath hoga,” to highlight former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru 's diplomatic legacy and its presence in the newly adopted Brics New Delhi Declaration.Congress leader Jairam Ramesh pointed to Paragraph 16 of the declaration, which recalls the 1955 Asian-African Conference in Bandung, Indonesia, and its principles of equality, independence, non-intervention and mutual benefit."Para 16 of the New Delhi Declaration just adopted at the Brics Summit says the following: 16. We recall 1955 Asian-African Conference in Bandung, Indonesia that proclaimed general principles, including equality, independence, non-intervention, and mutual benefit.”"We stress that the Bandung Spirit serves as a reference in the pursuit of a fairer, more inclusive, and representative multilateral system," he added.Jairam said the reference to Bandung in the Brics declaration showed how Nehru's vision for the Global South continues to resonate in contemporary diplomacy."Here are some jottings by Jawaharlal Nehru on the afternoon of April 22, 1955, at that historic meeting.Vineet Thakur recently wrote a fine piece on these and other jottings, doodles and notes of Nehru at Bandung. Remember that old Bollywood hit song Tu jahan jahan chale ga, mera saaya saath hoga," said the Congress leader.The Congress leader's reference to Bandung comes as Brics leaders push for reforms in global governance and greater representation for developing countries.Drawing on historian Vineet Thakur's analysis of Nehru's notes from the 1955 Bandung Conference, Jairam highlighted how the handwritten records captured the behind-the-scenes tensions and negotiations at the historic gathering.Nehru's notes included his observations on the length of speeches, including Carlos Romulo's 31.5-minute address, as well as his writings in Urdu, Hindi and English.The notes also recorded details that were not reflected in official accounts, including Ahmed al-Shukeiri's speech on Palestine, which helped place the issue within the emerging Global South agenda, ANI reported.Nehru also used the same airline pad slips to draft a tribute to Albert Einstein. Einstein had written to Nehru shortly before his death, urging him to engage with Chinese premier Zhou Enlai at Bandung to help ease tensions between China and the US over nuclear weapons.Earler in the day, the Brics countries adopted the New Delhi Declaration 2026, supporting the aspirations of India and Brazil to play a greater role in the United Nations, including its Security Council.China and Russia, both permanent members of the UN Security Council, reiterated their support for India's and Brazil's aspirations. Brics leaders also reaffirmed their commitment to reforming the Security Council to make it more democratic, representative, effective and efficient, with greater representation for developing countries.The declaration strongly condemned the April 2025 terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir and called for zero tolerance towards terrorism.On trade, the bloc expressed serious concern over the growing use of unilateral tariff and non-tariff measures, saying they distort trade, threaten global supply chains and create uncertainty for international economic activity.Brics also reaffirmed support for reform of the World Trade Organisation and called for an open, equitable, transparent, fair, inclusive and rules-based multilateral trading system. It called for the immediate restoration of a fully functioning two-tier binding WTO dispute settlement mechanism.In April 1955, representatives of 29 Asian and African governments gathered in Bandung, Indonesia, to discuss peace, economic development, decolonisation and the role of the developing world during the Cold War. The conference's core principles included political self-determination, respect for sovereignty, non-aggression, non-interference in internal affairs and equality.The Brics New Delhi Declaration was adopted at the 18th Brics Summit, being hosted by India. India's chairship is guided by the theme, “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.”
Article Summary: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh pointed to Paragraph 16 of the declaration, which recalls the 1955 Asian-African Conference in Bandung. "We stress that the Bandung Spirit serves as a reference in the pursuit of a fairer, more inclusive, and representative multilateral system," he added.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping held a bilateral meeting lasting more than 50 minutes in New Delhi on Saturday, shortly after the adoption of the Brics Summit 2026 declaration.The meeting took place on the sidelines of the Brics Summit, where leaders of the grouping adopted the summit declaration following discussions on key global and regional issues.Welcoming Xi, PM Modi thanked China for its support and cooperation during India's Brics chairmanship and said the two sides now had an opportunity to discuss bilateral ties."It gives me great pleasure to extend a warm welcome to you. He said the two countries, as the world's two most populous nations and key members of the Global South, have significant responsibilities amid a complex international landscape.Xi also said India and China should learn from each other's strengths and work towards shared development. During the meeting, he said:"In the face of a complex international landscape marked by intertwined changes and challenges, China and India, as the world's two most populous countries and important members of the Global South, shoulder significant responsibilities. Both sides should keep the future of humanity in mind and the well-being of their peoples at heart, and work together to advance high-quality cooperation within the greater BRICS framework. We should advocate an equal and orderly multipolar world and an inclusive, mutually beneficial form of economic globalisation, injecting more positive energy into the promotion of world peace, stability, development and prosperity."Earlier, the BRICS nations unanimously adopted the New Delhi Declaration 2026, which expressed deep concern over the continued escalation of tensions in West Asia and called for maximum restraint and avoidance of actions that could further aggravate the situation.“We urge to ensure the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure in accordance with the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations in their entirety and interconnectedness, including respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the States,” the declaration said.The BRICS declaration also encouraged greater efforts through dialogue and diplomacy towards a long-term understanding contributing to lasting peace, security and stability in the region.“We stress the need to work together to maintain smooth flow of global trade, supply chains and energy, in accordance with applicable international law,” it said.The grouping expressed serious concern over deliberate attacks on civilian infrastructure and peaceful nuclear facilities under full safeguards of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), stressing that nuclear safeguards, safety and security must be upheld, including during armed conflicts.The declaration also called for implementation of relevant UN General Assembly and UN Security Council resolutions and urged all parties to ensure the maintenance of ceasefire and full and unhindered humanitarian access in the Gaza Strip.Addressing the BRICS Summit, Xi Jinping called on BRICS nations to play a peacemaking role amid the conflict in West Asia, saying China would work with other members towards that goal.The BRICS declaration also noted the current global context of polarisation and distrust and encouraged global action to strengthen international peace and security. It advocated a multilateral approach that respects diverse national viewpoints on key global issues, including sustainable development, eradication of hunger and poverty and the global response to climate change.The grouping also expressed concern over growing nuclear risks and conflict and reiterated the need to strengthen the system of disarmament, arms control and non-proliferation to promote global stability and international peace and security.Earlier, addressing the 18th BRICS Summit session on Inclusive Global Governance and Strengthening in New Delhi, PM Modi proposed 10 measures for global governance reform, which BRICS members could develop into a BRICS Reform Roadmap by the next Summit.He also called for transforming the Global South from a “rule-taker into a rule-shaper”, saying the Global South remains at the forefront of global crises but continues to remain on the sidelines when it comes to decision-making.

PM Modi thanked China for its support and cooperation during India's Brics chairmanship.

Article Title: 'Zero tolerance' on terror: Brics declaration strongly condemns Pahalgam attack
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Brics countries have strongly condemned the Pahalgam terrorist attack in Jammu and Kashmir that killed 26 people, reaffirming their commitment to combating terrorism in all its forms and calling for “zero tolerance” towards the menace.The condemnation was included in the New Delhi Declaration 2026, adopted at the 18th Brics Summit in New Delhi on Saturday.The declaration also opposed double standards in countering terrorism and called for concerted action against all UN-designated terrorists and terrorist entities.“We express strong condemnation of any acts of terrorism as criminal and unjustifiable, regardless of their motivation, whenever, wherever and by whomsoever committed,” the declaration said.It specifically condemned “in the strongest terms” the terrorist attack in Jammu and Kashmir on April 22, 2025, during which 26 people were killed and several others injured.The Brics declaration reaffirmed the grouping’s commitment to combating terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, including the cross-border movement of terrorists, terrorism financing and safe havens.The grouping said terrorism should not be associated with any religion, nationality, civilisation or ethnic group.It also stressed that those involved in terrorist activities and their support must be held accountable and brought to justice in accordance with relevant national and international law.The declaration called for “zero tolerance for terrorism” and rejected double standards in countering terrorism.It also emphasised the primary responsibility of states in combating terrorism, while stressing that global efforts to prevent and counter terrorist threats must comply with international law, including the UN Charter and relevant international conventions and protocols.Brics welcomed the activities of its Counter-Terrorism Working Group and its five subgroups, which operate on the basis of the Brics Counter-Terrorism Strategy, Counter-Terrorism Action Plan and the Counter-Terrorism Working Group Position Paper.The grouping also called for the expeditious finalisation and adoption of the Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism under the UN framework.The declaration further stressed the importance of countering extremism and radicalisation, particularly among younger generations, and called for greater cooperation among Brics countries and their competent authorities, including through the sharing of best practices.On April 22, last year, 26 civilians were killed in a terrorist attack in the Baisaran meadow area near Pahalgam in South Kashmir, a major tourist destination.The victims were segregated by the attackers based on religion before being shot in front of their families, triggering widespread outrage.Security forces launched search operations in the surrounding areas following the attack, while investigations were expanded to trace the terrorist network and its logistical support.India responded with “Operation Sindoor” on May 7, 2025, carrying out precision strikes on terror infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.The operation marked a major escalation with Pakistan, followed by a four-day conflict that ended with a ceasefire on May 10, after Islamabad’s request.In the aftermath, Indian armed forces launched “Operation Mahadev” and tracked down and eliminated the three attackers involved in the Pahalgam killings.Beyond terrorism, the New Delhi Declaration reaffirmed Brics' support for comprehensive reform of the United Nations, including the UN Security Council, with greater representation for developing countries.China and Russia, as permanent members of the UN Security Council, reiterated their support for the aspirations of India and Brazil to play a greater role in the UN, including its Security Council.The declaration called for greater and more meaningful participation and representation of emerging market and developing countries, as well as Least Developed Countries, in global decision-making processes.On Security Council reform, Brics said the process should make the body more democratic, representative, effective and efficient while increasing the representation of developing countries.“We stress that the UN Security Council reform is to lead to the amplified voice of the Global South,” the declaration said.The grouping also called for equitable geographical representation in the UN Secretariat and other international organisations, particularly at senior and decision-making levels.The declaration also expressed serious concern over unilateral tariff and non-tariff measures, saying they distort trade, threaten global supply chains and create uncertainty for international economic activity.Brics reaffirmed its support for reform of the World Trade Organization and called for an open, equitable, transparent, fair, inclusive, predictable and rules-based multilateral trading system, with the WTO at its core.The grouping also advocated the immediate restoration of an accessible, effective and fully functioning two-tier binding WTO dispute settlement mechanism and called for the appointment of new Appellate Body members without further delay.On unilateral coercive measures, Brics condemned sanctions that it said were contrary to international law and reiterated its opposition to unilateral coercive measures, including those not authorised by the UN Security Council.The New Delhi Declaration was adopted during the 18th Brics Summit, being hosted by India on September 12-13 under its 2026 chairship. India’s Brics chairship is guided by the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.”
Article Summary: Brics countries have strongly condemned the Pahalgam terrorist attack in Jammu and Kashmir that killed 26 people. The condemnation was included in the New Delhi Declaration 2026, adopted at the 18th Brics Summit in New Delhi on Saturday. The declaration also opposed double standards in countering terrorism.

Article Title: Air India pilot dies during Delhi layover
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: A Mumbai-based Air India pilot died during a Delhi layover on Friday. The pilot, in his 40s, had recently moved from Air India Express to AI. He was found unconscious at his room in The Gran, Vasant Kunj, and rushed to a hospital where he was declared dead.“Air India is deeply saddened at the passing away of a cockpit crew member in Delhi last night. He was on a layover rest at a hotel in Delhi where he was found unconscious last evening. He was rushed to the hospital immediately, where he was declared dead. Air India is in close touch with his family and is extending all support at this time of grief,” an AI spokesperson said.Delhi Police said the pilot had checked into the hotel on Thursday. On Friday evening his brother contacted the hotel manager, saying he was not responding to calls. “The hotel manager went to the pilot’s room and found it locked from inside. The room was opened with the help of hotel master key. (He) was found lying unconscious and unresponsive,” said the police.“The deceased’s post-mortem examination was conducted at Safdarjung Hospital on Saturday. The final cause of death shall be ascertained after receipt of the final opinion. Further enquiry is in progress,” the police added.

NEW DELHI: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), in coordination with the ministry of external affairs (MEA), ministry of home affairs (MHA) and Punjab Police, has secured the extradition of Red Notice subject Amritpal Singh alias Gurpal Singh from Moldova to India, the agency said.Singh is wanted in multiple serious criminal cases in Punjab, including double murder using firearms and offences under the Arms Act and NDPS Act. His criminal antecedents also include cases related to forgery, cheating, use of forged documents and violations of the Passport Act, according to the CBI.The extradition followed a request from Punjab Police, after which the CBI secured an Interpol Red Notice against Singh. The team, along with Singh, arrived in Delhi on September 12.Singh, also known as Amrit Dalam, was among the most wanted gangsters linked to the Jaggu Bhagwanpuria gang.The report said he was detained near the Moldova border based on an Interpol Red Notice issued at the request of Punjab Police in coordination with the MEA, CBI and other central agencies.He’s a native of Dalam Nangal village in Batala and had fled India using a fake passport and was allegedly making extortion calls to businessmen, particularly in the Amritsar region.Punjab Police had also established the Overseas Fugitive Tracking and Extradition Cell (OFTEC), headed by IG-Counterintelligence Ashish Choudhary, to track criminals hiding abroad and pursue their extradition to Punjab.Punjab DGP Gaurav Yadav had said Singh was wanted in several serious cases, including murder, attempted murder and drug smuggling.He had also said Singh's detention followed international coordination and follow-up by Punjab Police agencies, while legal and diplomatic procedures were being pursued for his extradition or deportation to India.The latest extradition brings Singh back to India to face the criminal cases registered against him in Punjab.

NEW DELHI: The Brics countries on Saturday unanimously adopted the New Delhi Declaration 2026 at the 18th Brics Summit in New Delhi. The 45-page declaration, comprising 140 points, was discussed under the theme “Strengthening Cooperation to Promote Fair Competition, including in Renewable Energy Markets”, with the aim of supporting sustainable energy transitions.“No member has raised any objection. The New Delhi Declaration 2026 is adopted unanimously,” PM Modi said at the summit.The declaration focused on condemning terrorism, conflict prevention and peaceful resolution of disputes, stronger multilateralism and concerns over unilateral trade measures.PM Modi, in his separate opening remarks, called for reforms in global governance and proposed 10 measures to be developed into a Brics reform roadmap. He also called for greater representation of the Global South in international decision-making, describing the existing system as a “pyramid of privilege” that should become a “platform of partnership”.The declaration was adopted on the first day of the two-day Summit being hosted by India in New Delhi. The joint declaration came after intensive negotiations that continued until 4 am on Saturday, with India leading efforts to bridge differences between the UAE and Iran over the Middle East conflict.The talks followed an earlier Brics foreign ministers’ meeting under India’s presidency that ended without a consensus, prompting prolonged negotiations to ensure the summit resulted in a joint statement.India is chairing Brics in 2026 under the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”.The Declaration addressed various key issues and concerns affecting the global order, such as:Brics strongly condemned terrorism in all forms, including cross-border terrorism, terrorism financing and safe havens, condemned the April 22, 2025, terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir, and called for zero tolerance, accountability and early adoption of the UN Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism. "We reaffirm our commitment to combating terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, including the cross-border movement of terrorists, terrorism financing and safe havens," it said."We reiterate that terrorism should not be associated with any religion, nationality, civilization or ethnic group and that all those involved in terrorist activities and their support must be held accountable and brought to justice in accordance with relevant national and international law," it continued, adding, ""We urge to ensure zero tolerance for terrorism and reject double standards in countering terrorism. "The bloc reaffirmed its commitment to mutual respect, sovereign equality, solidarity, inclusiveness and consensus, and pledged to strengthen cooperation across its three pillars: political and security, economic and financial, and cultural and people-to-people cooperation. "We commend India for hosting the Outreach/BRICS Plus Dialogue segment of the 18thBRICS Summit, which injects new impetus to strengthen international cooperation andsolidarity," it further statedBrics countries stressed the importance of efforts to prevent conflicts, including by addressing their root causes. The declaration reaffirmed a commitment to resolving disputes through dialogue, consultation and diplomacy. Brics further urged all parties to uphold the Gaza ceasefire and ensure unhindered humanitarian aid, opposed the forced displacement of Palestinians, and reaffirmed support for a two-state solution with an independent Palestinian state based on the internationally recognised 1967 borders."We express deep concern over the ​continued escalation of tensions in Middle East...call for exercising maximum restraint...avoiding actions that could further aggravate the situation."Drugs and arms traffickingBrics expressed concern over illicit financial flows linked to drug-related crimes, firearms trafficking, terrorism financing and organised crime, and called for stronger cross-border cooperation to trace and disrupt criminal proceeds. “We express our concerns about illicit financial flows including, financing of terrorism, trafficking of firearms, trafficking in persons, the laundering of drug related crimes proceeds,” the declaration said.Brics voiced concern over unilateral tariff and non-tariff measures, warning they could hurt global trade and disrupt supply chains. “We voice serious concerns about the rise of unilateral tariff and non-tariff measures which distort trade and are inconsistent with WTO rules,” the declaration said.It reaffirmed support for a WTO-centred multilateral trading system and called for the immediate restoration of a “fully functioning, two-tier binding WTO dispute settlement mechanism”, along with the appointment of new Appellate Body members. The bloc also condemned unilateral economic and secondary sanctions. “We condemn the imposition of unilateral coercive measures that are contrary to international law,” the declaration said, calling for their elimination as they “undermine international law and the principles and purposes of the UN Charter. ”It also backed Ethiopia and Iran’s WTO membership bids and noted China’s move to extend zero-tariff treatment to 53 African countries with which it has diplomatic ties.The declaration called for stronger energy security through diversified energy sources, resilient infrastructure and stable markets, while recognising that fossil fuels will continue to play an important role, particularly for emerging and developing economies. “We acknowledge fossil fuels will still play an important role in the world's energy mix, particularly for emerging markets and developing economies (EMDEs),” it said. It also backed “just, orderly, equitable and inclusive energy transitions” and a technology-neutral approach covering renewables, nuclear energy, hydropower, hydrogen, fossil fuels and low-carbon technologies.Brics recognised women as leaders, decision-makers and drivers of economic growth and social transformation, stressing their participation in governance, economic life, peacebuilding and climate action."We affirm that women's participation in governance; their financial and digital inclusion; their capacity building, access to skill development and entrepreneurship opportunities, support to entrepreneurship, access to productive and social services and their crucial role in climate action, food security and nutrition, which are interconnected is key for sustainable development," the declaration said."We also recognise the importance of policies that support women's full participation in economic life, including through appropriate care policies, in accordance with national circumstances," the leaders further said.Brics backed efforts to promote cross-border payments and trade settlements using member countries’ local currencies, while respecting national priorities. “We acknowledge the work done to study the cross-border interoperability of payment and messaging channels, and the discussions on promoting trade settlements and investments using BRICS local currencies,” the declaration stated.Brics reaffirmed support for reform of the UN, including the Security Council, to make it more democratic and representative and give developing countries a greater role. China and Russia, as permanent members of the Security Council, reiterated their support for Brazil and India to play a greater role in the UN, including its Security Council. “China and Russia, as permanent members of the UN Security Council, reiterate their support to the aspirations of Brazil and India to play a greater role in the UN, including its Security Council,” the declaration said.Brics recognised the growing role of technology in improving sports performance, athlete welfare, governance and inclusion, and encouraged greater cooperation among member countries through exchanges of good practices, technical information and research. “We welcome the proposal for the BRICS Sports Goods Manufacturing Conclave to promote cooperation in sports goods manufacturing, research and innovation,” the declaration stated. It also encouraged discussions on forming a dedicated Working Group on Sports Technology.
Article Summary: The 45-page declaration, comprising 140 points, was discussed under the theme “Strengthening Cooperation to Promote Fair Competition, including in Renewable Energy Markets” The declaration focused on condemning terrorism, conflict prevention and peaceful resolution of disputes, stronger multilateralism and concerns over unilateral trade measures.

Article Title: Strategic Autonomy in motion as India hosts 18th BRICS Summit
Article Text:
This would be the 18th summit of the grouping. (Photo: ANI)

India for BRICS

Key Challenges for India
